EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East faces significant escalation risks, primarily centered on the Strait of Hormuz where conflicting claims of control and US military actions have emerged, coinciding with a new US-Venezuela oil deal. Concurrently, Israel continues targeted strikes against Hamas in Gaza for ceasefire violations and faces internal and international condemnation for escalating settler violence in the West Bank.

IRAN
Iranian security forces conducted operations in Sistan and Baluchestan province, killing one and capturing six terrorists from the Jaish al-Adl group. A weapons and ammunition shipment was also discovered and seized on the Iranian-Iraqi border in Kurdistan province. Air defense activity, possibly fireworks, was reported in Tehran (Starokhan, Enghelab Square) on the eve of Prophet Muhammad's birth anniversary. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian congratulated Islamic countries on the Prophet's birthday, emphasizing peace and security, and stated that implementing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the US from June would prevent chaos in West Asia. Pezeshkian also announced plans to raise unsubsidized fuel prices to 10,000 Tomans per liter due to "war" conditions blocking import routes. Acting Defense Minister Brig. Gen. Seyyed Majid Ibn Al-Reza affirmed Iran's commitment to constantly boosting military capabilities for deterrence. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf publicly mocked US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, accusing him of lying and failing to manage markets, particularly concerning oil transit in the Strait of Hormuz. The dollar price in Iran reached 206,000 Tomans. The US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) suspended General License G, leading to the Duolingo English Test (DET) becoming unavailable for Iranians and reports of TOEFL cancellations, severely impacting Iranian students. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi asserted that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and will not reopen until Washington fulfills commitments under the "Islamabad memorandum," dismissing US claims of oil transit as psychological warfare to manipulate energy prices. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard Navy claims full control of the Strait of Hormuz and will not allow passage without coordination.

ISRAEL
The IDF killed three Hamas operatives in Gaza in two separate strikes. Yesterday, August 29, 2026, Hani Abd al-Hai Fakhri Mazloum, a company commander in Hamas's elite Nukhba Force, and Hassan Zidan Hassan Deiri, a Hamas sniper, were killed in northern Gaza. Both were involved in weapons trafficking and advancing terror plots, violating the ceasefire. A separate strike in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, targeted another Hamas commander hiding adjacent to Shuhada al-Aqsa Hospital, who was also advancing terror plots and attempting to restore Hamas capabilities in violation of the ceasefire. Israeli artillery fire was reported in the Damascus countryside near Beit Jan. An alleged ramming attempt near a military training base in the Jordan Valley led to its closure. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Isaac Herzog strongly condemned violent acts by Israeli rioters in Qusra and Jalud, calling them a "red line" and urging law enforcement to act decisively. US Ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, also called for "decisive action" to back these statements. Shin Bet confirmed the urgent evacuation of PM Netanyahu's son, Yair Netanyahu, from the US to Israel due to a "significant threat to assassinate him." Domestically, there was political maneuvering as Yair Lapid and Avigdor Lieberman met to coordinate pre-election strategies. Minister Itamar Ben Gvir publicly criticized PM Netanyahu, accusing him of orchestrating a "cynical game" regarding unity talks with other right-wing parties. Multiple incidents of shooting, car accidents, and wildfires were reported across Israel, including a shooting incident in Rahat where a 25-year-old man was critically injured, and two fatal shootings in Jaffa. Ultra-Orthodox demonstrators blocked the entrance to Jerusalem, causing heavy traffic.

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF operations in Gaza resulted in the killing of three Hamas operatives, including a Nukhba company commander, a sniper, and another commander involved in terror plots and rebuilding capabilities. Palestinian sources reported one person injured by IDF fire in Shuja'iyya. A Palestinian rights organization estimates that between 2,500 and 3,000 Palestinians have been forcibly disappeared during Israel's war on Gaza. Three young Palestinians were reportedly killed in an Israeli drone strike in Jenin. In the West Bank, dozens of Israeli rioters threw stones and barricaded themselves in a Palestinian house in Qusra, injuring a Palestinian woman. Similar incidents were reported in Jalud, where Israeli settlers also attacked NBC journalists. The IDF stated that Hamas operatives were systematically violating the ceasefire by advancing terror plots and operating near humanitarian infrastructure like Shuhada al-Aqsa Hospital.

LEBANON
The IDF renewed fire attacks in Al-Mansouri, southern Lebanon, and conducted strikes against a building in Houla and other areas in Ayta al-Jabal. Israeli forces also attacked the strategic Ali al-Taher heights, overlooking Nabatiyeh, with what Lebanese media reported as phosphorus bombs. Press TV cited Israeli aggression continuing with fresh attacks and airstrikes in southern areas, including Al-Nabatya Al-Fawqa. Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabiih Berri stated that there is no alternative to the presence of international forces in southern Lebanon as long as Israel refuses to adhere to the "framework agreement."

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, reports indicated Israeli artillery fire toward the Beit Jan area in the western Damascus countryside. A Britain-based war monitor stated that Israeli forces have conducted over 1,000 incursions into southern Syria since the fall of the Assad government in December 2024. A powerful dust storm turned the sky orange over Homs. In Iraq, Kata'ib Sayyid al-Shuhada resistance group declared it would place its weapons under state control, but only on the condition of US forces withdrawal. The Iraqi Prime Minister's security advisor, Qassem al-Araji, stated that the presence of PKK forces on Iraqi soil is illegal and that Iraq is working with Turkey to resolve the issue. He also noted that Iran emphasized the need to expel extremist groups from Iraq. Al-Araji affirmed that Iraq's interests are paramount, balancing relations with both Iran and the US. He also mentioned that the withdrawal of the international coalition (US) from Iraq on September 30 would not sever ties with the US. A colonel in the Peshmerga reported that the US Treasury decided to halt financial aid to Peshmerga due to the Kurdistan Regional Government's (KRG) failure to comply with US direction regarding Peshmerga unification. A fuel station in Duhok, Iraqi Kurdistan, was engulfed in fire, reportedly linked to black market petrol trade.

GULF STATES
The US CENTCOM claimed successful mine-clearing operations in the Strait of Hormuz, announcing that Iranian naval mines had been removed from international shipping lanes, and traffic in the southern channels had increased. US President Donald Trump declared the Strait of Hormuz "under our control" and warned that any vessels attempting to lay new mines would be destroyed. Iran, however, disputed these claims, with its Revolutionary Guard stating full control of Hormuz and denying passage without coordination. A security source quoted by Press TV labeled US claims as a ploy to manipulate global energy prices. An Emirati ship reportedly attempted to cross the southern Strait of Hormuz but failed and returned. In Bahrain, large crowds protested against the Al Khalifa regime's trial of Shia scholars and civil rights abuses. The UAE Central Bank is reportedly reviewing the status of "Bank Misr" branches over potential reputational risks. Qatar's Foreign Minister held a phone conversation with his Turkish counterpart to discuss de-escalation efforts. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister stated that Iran has reached an understanding with Oman regarding transit arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz, but its implementation depends on the US fulfilling its commitments. Egypt and Italy jointly called for regional de-escalation and the preservation of maritime security and freedom of navigation. Goldman Sachs estimated that oil flow from the Strait of Hormuz has reached two-thirds of pre-war levels, at 7-8 million barrels per day.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Strait of Hormuz Conflict**: US CENTCOM claimed successful clearing of Iranian naval mines and reopening of southern shipping lanes, with President Trump declaring the Strait "under our control." Iran's Revolutionary Guard and Deputy FM Gharibabadi disputed this, asserting continued Iranian control and dismissing US claims as psychological warfare.
2.  **US-Venezuela Oil Deal**: US President Donald Trump announced an "historic" agreement with Venezuela's Interim President Delcy Rodriguez, granting the US majority control over 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves. Venezuela expects over $100 billion in investments and $209 billion in tax revenue over 25 years, aiming for 1.5 million barrels/day.
3.  **Israeli Strikes in Gaza**: IDF killed three Hamas operatives/commanders (Hani Abd al-Hai Fakhri Mazloum, Hassan Zidan Hassan Deiri, and another commander) in separate strikes in northern and central Gaza, citing violations of the ceasefire.
4.  **Israeli Settler Violence in West Bank**: Incidents of Israeli rioters throwing stones and barricading in a Palestinian house in Qusra, injuring a Palestinian woman, with similar events in Jalud. PM Netanyahu, President Herzog, and US Ambassador Huckabee strongly condemned these actions.
5.  **US Sanctions Impact on Iranian Education**: The US OFAC suspended General License G, leading to the unavailability of Duolingo English Test for Iranians and reported cancellations of TOEFL exams, severely affecting Iranian students seeking international education.
6.  **Israeli Strikes in Southern Lebanon**: IDF renewed strikes in Al-Mansouri, Houla, and Ayta al-Jabal, southern Lebanon. Reports included the use of phosphorus bombs on Ali al-Taher heights near Nabatiyeh.
7.  **Yair Netanyahu Evacuation**: Shin Bet confirmed the urgent evacuation of PM Netanyahu's son, Yair Netanyahu, from the US due to a "significant threat to assassinate him."
8.  **Iraqi Militia Disarmament Talks**: Iraqi officials, including PM's security advisor al-Araji, discussed disarming militias. Kata'ib Sayyid al-Shuhada stated it would hand over weapons only if US forces withdraw. The US reportedly cut financial aid to Peshmerga.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, where conflicting claims of control, alleged US mine-clearing operations, and potential for US military deployments (e.g., USS Theodore Roosevelt) create a volatile flashpoint. The US-Venezuela oil deal could further antagonize Iran, linking energy prices directly to regional stability. Continued Israeli military operations in Gaza and southern Lebanon, including the reported use of phosphorus bombs, risk wider regional conflict. The West Bank continues to be an active flashpoint due to escalating settler violence, which has drawn strong condemnations from Israeli and US leadership but lacks immediate enforcement details. Iran's firm stance on controlling Hormuz and its commitment to boosting military capabilities signal a readiness for confrontation.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is characterized by asserting control over the Strait of Hormuz, securing oil supplies through the Venezuela deal, and implementing sanctions against Iran. US Ambassador Huckabee urged Israel to take "decisive action" regarding settler violence. The US is also planning to withdraw its international coalition forces from Iraq by September 30. Qatar and Turkey are engaged in diplomatic efforts for de-escalation and stability. Egypt and Italy have called for de-escalation in West Asia and safeguarding maritime security. Russia is focused on its war in Ukraine, with new ground offensives planned for Kyiv and Chernihiv, and its state media discusses nuclear threats against Britain. China is involved in aid efforts for Nepal but has no direct reported involvement in the Middle East conflict in the past 24 hours. The UAE saw a ship reportedly attempt and fail to traverse the southern Strait of Hormuz, highlighting ongoing maritime challenges.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding the Strait of Hormuz: US CENTCOM claims success in mine-clearing and reopening southern lanes, with President Trump declaring control, while Iranian sources firmly deny this, asserting continued closure and Iranian control. These conflicting narratives appear to be part of a broader psychological warfare campaign aimed at manipulating energy markets. Unverified claims include the imminent deployment of the USS Theodore Roosevelt and impending war, which, if true, would dramatically alter the threat landscape. Reports of "air defense activity" in Tehran were also contested by claims of fireworks, highlighting a lack of clarity on internal security events. Propaganda indicators are evident in both Iranian and Israeli state media, with Iran portraying US actions as failures and manipulations, and Israel emphasizing Hamas's ceasefire violations and use of human shields. Reporting gaps include the specific details of the "Islamabad memorandum," the precise nature of the "significant threat" against Yair Netanyahu, and comprehensive, independently verifiable data on the scale of US mine-clearing operations in Hormuz. Information regarding the alleged "Barzani gangs" in Iraqi Kurdistan involved in black market petrol is also unverified.
